name: Site map / URL discovery
gap: Quarry /v1/map caps limit at 1000, does not read robots Sitemap: lines, has no index or SERP assist, and ranks lexically; /v1/map is user-token-only so the Model Plane cannot call it.
strengths: Shipped end to end with a CrawlPagePicker UI and robots allow-filtering (which Firecrawl's map does not emphasise).

name: Web search API with filters, categories and provider fallback
gap: Minor: no category shortcuts (pdf/github/research) or per-source option objects; find-similar has no UI caller; confirm include/exclude domains are post-filtered on results and not only sent as site: operators (search_r…
strengths: Ahead: multi-provider smart router (Tantivy, Stract, SearXNG, Brave, Serper plus Data Plane vectors) with ZDR gating, Tavily-style params (topic, time_range, chunks_per_source, highlight, facets, intent), image/video/si…

name: Agent web tools with citations and per-URL network permission
gap: Model Plane web_search/web_fetch are read-only with no approval gate; no evidence of an org-level per-URL allow/deny policy applied at tool level (Quarry applies SSRF/security preflight and blocklists exist in control);…
strengths: Tools are shipped over Quarry with ZDR propagated in the request body (web_tools.rs search_body/extract_body carry zdr).

name: Uniform machine-readable error envelope
gap: Quarry's envelope is flat {error, code, hint, window, retry_after_seconds, next_actions} while the Verevon gateway rule is {error:{code,message,details}}; confirm the gateway maps consistently (INF, not verified).
strengths: Shipped (SRC): quarry-edge api_error.rs:11-26 ApiError with retry_after_seconds and next_actions; quarry-core error.rs:10-50 ErrorCode with retryable() and http_status(), including browser-specific codes (ActionUnknown,…

name: Team usage, concurrency and queue endpoints
gap: Values depend on billing integration (baseline section 1 says forwarding only); not verified that numbers are populated in prod.
strengths: SRC: resource_routes.rs:836-935 implements /v1/team/{credit-usage,token-usage,concurrency,queue-status,activity} forwarding to control. Parity on the surface.

name: HTML to Markdown conversion and agent web-fetch
gap: Minor: markdown quality of the html2md path vs a GFM-table-aware converter is unverified; base64-image stripping not confirmed.
strengths: Native Rust conversion inside the Ingestion Plane (no extra service hop), charset sniffing, soft-404 detection and body cap; gateway preview falls back to /v1/extract markdown.

name: Rich rendering of agent output (diagrams, code, math, file previews, citations)
gap: Highlighter is an in-house dependency-free one (fewer languages than Shiki).
strengths: KaTeX math, Mermaid rendering gated on a closed fence (avoids streaming parse errors), code highlighting, CSV artifacts and grouped web citations are shipped (SRC, verified in this pass; no baseline record).

name: Domain-shaped extraction formats (product, menu)
gap: No menu shape (not relevant to Verevon's B2B focus).
strengths: Product extraction and summary ship with a picker UI; structured harvest (JSON-LD, hydration) supplies product data without an LLM.

name: Provider-agnostic model routing for content LLM features
gap: Quarry's access is disabled by the shipped cross-plane token manifest (model-invoke false); that grant gap is tracked under C-t2-02-009.
strengths: Verevon centralises routing, fallback and ZDR-aware provider selection in the Model Plane, which is architecturally stronger than per-service routing (SRC: file presence only, not read in depth).

name: Multi-tier fetch engine core (HTTP, TLS-impersonating HTTP and headless browser behind one interface)
gap: No Firefox/WebKit engines (Chromium only); otherwise equivalent.
strengths: Static (pinned DNS, per-hop redirect validation), TLS-impersonation and local chromiumoxide drivers already sit behind one FallbackDriver; this is at or above Firecrawl OSS. Keep the single trait and per-hop SSRF valida…

name: SSRF containment for browser traffic
gap: None versus references.
strengths: Per-session DNS-pinned loopback egress proxy (resolve once and connect to the pinned IP, closing the rebinding window), CDP Fetch guard, --disable-quic, per-hop redirect validation and egress receipts. Keep, and require…

name: Console capture and page-level debugging aids
gap: No drag-and-drop helper action (minor).
strengths: CDP-level collectors for console, log, request, response and lifecycle (no page-script patching, so pages cannot tamper) plus a DevTools drawer (console/dom/network/vision) in the UI: ahead of Aside's in-page intercepto…

name: Proxy pool plumbing and egress self-check
gap: No user-facing egress self-check (which IP/proxy served this run) beyond per-session redacted egress receipts; no published static egress IP list for customer allow-listing.
strengths: QUARRY_PROXY_POOL (socks5/socks5h/http/https) with sticky (org,host) hashing, processor-approval gating via PrivacyPolicy, per-agent-run proxy affinity and DNS-pinned browser egress proxy is richer than either reference…

name: Localized SERP retrieval (Google SERP proxy)
gap: Equivalent outcome via search-provider APIs (country/language params per baseline) rather than SERP scraping; no gap worth closing.
strengths: Provider circuit breakers and TTL cache; API providers avoid scraping Google, which is cleaner for compliance.

name: Politeness and throughput throttling
gap: No user-settable per-job maxRequestsPerMinute/maxConcurrency, and robots Crawl-delay is not fed into the scheduler; the live Go crawl is one page at a time.
strengths: AIMD per-host HostScheduler plus global AutoscaledPool wired into PageRunner is ahead of both references.

name: SSRF and private-network egress defences
gap: Minor: /v1/extract and /v1/map skip SecurityEngine.preflight (rely on driver DNS guard, INF); add a post-connect remote-address assertion as a second layer and apply the guard to tenant webhook URLs when webhooks are ex…
strengths: DNS resolve-once-and-pin, redirect re-validation, per-session pinned browser egress proxy with CDP Fetch guard, QUIC disabled and redacted egress receipts: best in class. Keep and extend to webhooks.

name: Domain blocklists (global and per org) with exceptions and hit logging
gap: Org-scoped keyword/regex exceptions and blocked-hit logging are not confirmed in the baseline (check blocklists.go).
strengths: Control-plane managed blocklists plus an edge security snapshot exist.

name: Request idempotency for mutating calls
gap: No baseline record; spot-check (SRC): edge stamps an Idempotency-Key on every mutating call to control with a comment that control must dedupe (org, key, route); events carry idempotency_key. Not verified whether contro…
strengths: Internal edge->control idempotency is already more deliberate than Firecrawl's reject-on-reuse.

name: Durable request queue / URL frontier with lease-based multi-consumer claims
gap: Core primitives exist (Postgres SKIP LOCKED queue, priority, visibility timeouts, job idempotency keys). Weaker points: the durable frontier is only used when the orchestrator has edge URL/token/secret configured, other…
strengths: Keep the Rust PostgresRequestQueue plus Temporal durability and deterministic job idempotency; this is on par with Firecrawl's NuQ for Verevon's scale and avoids a second queue store.

name: Bulk crawl/batch/schedule engine alongside the interactive browser
gap: Engine exists but its crawl semantics are weak (see C-t2-05-007, -008, -010).
strengths: Verevon combines both halves (Quarry crawl/map/batch/schedules + interactive agent browser) which neither Codex nor Aside has; keep bulk acquisition out of the agent tab loop.

name: Tool quality/trust score for ranking and selection
gap: No baseline record; found in code during this comparison (SRC, light read): capability-core computes a deterministic composite rank from success_rate, schema_fail_rate, p95 latency, mean cost, approval_rate, incident_co…
strengths: Pure, unit-testable composite score with per-call weight overrides, already oriented to agent tool selection rather than marketplace popularity.

name: Organization accounts with member permissions and central billing
gap: Minor: quarry-control webhooks are not org-scoped (v-quarry-107 note).
strengths: Control Plane orgs/identity/billing; every web/browser route derives org from the verified session; Quarry enforces JWT org, actor-scoped runs and tenant-stamped artifacts.

name: Agent configuration sync across devices with conflict resolution
gap: Not needed by architecture: Verevon agent skills/config are server-side (session-core) and therefore identical on every device (INF from server-side skill storage). Concurrent-edit conflict UX for shared skills not veri…
strengths: Server-side org/user agent configuration avoids device sync entirely.

name: Tenant-registered search corpora and saved search configurations
gap: Saved named search configurations (provider mix per Space) are not a distinct object; tension noted between Quarry local Tantivy index and the no-retrieval-plane rule (v-quarry-093 INF).
strengths: Durable org-scoped sources registry, local org-scoped corpus index skipped under ZDR, hybrid search with Data Plane vectors + rerank (RRF), and four SERP providers with paid-provider and ZDR switches go beyond the visib…

name: Managed egress proxy with domain policy and destination validation
gap: Server-side header or credential injection by secret reference is missing (pairs with C-t2-07-015).
strengths: Verevon is at or ahead of parity: governed allowed_domains come only from the broker grant, domains are checked before and after each action, agent runs are refused unless the driver proves isolated egress, egress recei…

name: Operator health, readiness and setup diagnostics
gap: Optional: there is no agent- or user-callable 'why can't this browser session start' diagnostic for remote providers.
strengths: Readiness reports durability; production refuses ephemeral stores and default control keys; internal control uses HMAC rather than path secrets (ahead of Firecrawl).

name: Self-host stack with hardened browser container
gap: To check: whether the edge container has cap_drop, no-new-privileges, tmpfs and resource limits equivalent to Firecrawl's playwright-service (not confirmed in the baseline).
strengths: Verevon is ahead on defaults: production refuses ephemeral stores and default control keys, Chromium is pinned, and the stack is complete (postgres, dragonfly, temporal, control, orchestrator, searxng).

name: Operations console for runs, schedules, storage and integrations
gap: The fleet console is a stub that calls an unrouted /v1/fleets (see C-t2-07-011).
strengths: An Ingestions console with runs, schedules, monitoring, sources, evidence and profiles, plus an ingestion section in Insights.

name: Browser profiles and persistent login state
strengths: Verevon is ahead on governance: profile CRUD with scope, restore probe, ZDR chip, and ZDR forbidding persistent profiles. Keep scope separation and never widen via Space.

name: Agent-control indicator, live view and human take-over
gap: Minor: the WebSocket live/takeover channel is a stub (liveFrameWsUrl null; frames via 700 ms poll or SSE); no per-tab 'AI controlling' badge or Esc-to-cancel; no shareable read-only live-view link for teammates.
strengths: Control-mode switching is authoritative in Quarry (agent actions get 409 during takeover), human input auto-switches to takeover, and direct pointer/wheel/keyboard on the frame works. Keep authority in Quarry.

name: Readable tool-call transcript and work log
strengths: Timeline + evidence drawer with typed artifact viewer, per-step rationale and Quarry receipt replay is ahead of a plain transcript. Keep it; surface it inside chat runs too.

name: Agent incognito / ephemeral sessions
strengths: ZDR goes further: pre-session toggle, always-visible chip, server guard, no persistent profiles, artifacts withheld, vision summary skipped, local history purged, model-gateway refuses runs under issuer-enforced ZDR. Ke…

name: Typed backend-agnostic command protocol with per-backend capability discovery
gap: Capability matrix is enforced fail-closed in Quarry; check that execution-core surfaces driver capabilities to the model (see C06).
strengths: Typed Rust AgentAction contracts plus fail-closed driver capability gating are on par with Codex.

name: Accessibility-tree observation with stable element refs and diffs
gap: None material. Verify that deltas are returned to the model by default after each act (baseline says deltas exist in the observation protocol).
strengths: Quarry binds refs to CDP backend node ids from the native AX tree (stronger than injected-script refs) and discloses frames origin-only.

name: Stale-target protection and ref re-resolution
gap: Fail-closed is shipped (TARGET_REPAIR_REQUIRED). Missing only the optional Aside-style unique re-resolution by signature, which would save a re-observe round-trip.
strengths: Fail-closed stale detection with frame-execution-context checks matches Codex.

name: Playwright-compatible semantic locators across frames with failure diagnostics
gap: Check whether ambiguous/no-match errors include candidate samples like Codex.
strengths: Semantic locators with fail-closed ambiguity and explicit OOPIF frame actions are shipped.

name: JavaScript dialog handling as controllable objects
gap: None.
strengths: Never auto-resolved and requires a one-shot approval grant scoped to the exact dialog: stricter than Aside's auto-accept.

name: Crash-safe runs: recovery, persistent suspensions and rerun-safe tool classification
gap: Check that resume treats an in-flight non-idempotent action (submit, click) as 'unsettled' rather than replaying it. ZDR runs have no resume by design.
strengths: Immutable step receipts, checkpoints and resume with Postgres queue.

name: Durable human-in-the-loop approvals with fail-closed semantics
gap: Check headless/scheduled runs map 'ask' to deny rather than hanging.
strengths: Risk-classified approvals reuse generic orchestration approvals and fail closed; Quarry one-shot grants are scoped to exact frame/dialog/artifact and reject replay.

name: Risk-tier confirmation taxonomy and final-confirm mode with typed review artifacts
gap: Risk classes (login, checkout, posting_form, destructive, cross-domain, persistent cookie) are shipped; typed draft previews and a per-session 'ask first' switch are unverified.
strengths: Fail-closed, code-enforced classification (not prompt-only like part of Codex's DOC taxonomy).

name: Navigation guard: scheme allowlist and request-level interception of redirects, subframes and popups
gap: Certificate-interstitial handling not verified.
strengths: Quarry installs a fail-closed CDP Fetch guard before navigation that covers redirects, frames, XHR and subresources with deny-all default, and allows only http/https (SRC, read in this audit): equal to Codex.

name: Visual proof and recording of agent work
gap: No video recording artifact; immutable receipts and proof bundles cover evidence.
strengths: Proof bundle, immutable step receipts, browser timeline and live frames exceed both references' evidence model.

name: Task record and replay of browser procedures
gap: Quarry compiles procedures and runs replay/quality/impact checks, but has no procedure store or execute endpoint and Verevon does not call them.
strengths: Verevon is ahead of all references here (procedure compile and replay checks exist in code).

name: Bot-detection and CAPTCHA reporting with strict no-bypass scope
gap: Ensure challenge signals map to a user hand-off (C19).
strengths: Challenge signals are part of every observation.

name: Server-side credential-injecting connector proxy for agents
gap: Minor: access is scoped per connection/org/user rather than per run (no run-lifetime proxy token); connector actions are a curated static catalog rather than admin-configurable per-connection allow-lists.
strengths: Equal or ahead: first-party OAuth broker for about 25 providers, encrypted vault, short-lived internal token broker, named whitelisted operations only (raw proxy returns 410), approval-gated writes with signed attestati…

name: MCP client endpoint hardening (HTTPS-only, no redirects, tool permission rules)
gap: None material.
strengths: Ahead of Aside: no redirects plus DNS pinning per dial, SSRF re-validation of discovery/DCR/token hops, periodic DNS revalidation with quarantine, a mandatory exact tool allowlist, and mcp__<server>__<tool> namespacing …

name: Idempotent, receipted (and metered) provider action execution
gap: No per-action price quote or credit reservation for paid provider calls (billing is usage-metered elsewhere); read actions are not idempotency-tracked (acceptable).
strengths: Ahead: mandatory idempotency keys on writes, request-hash conflict detection, signed attestation of the acting user, receipt states including unknown, all inside an audit transaction drained to Audit Core. Keep.

name: Scraped and synced data into knowledge stores and destinations
gap: Into Verevon's own Data Plane: shipped (IC handoff; Quarry ingest via the Data Plane contract per v-quarry baseline section 6). External destinations (warehouses, external vector DBs) are absent, which is acceptable for…
strengths: Tenant-isolated ingest through the Data Plane contract respects ZDR and the no-cross-plane-DB rule; do not adopt a cross-tenant shared scrape cache.

name: Partner/user provisioning API
gap: None relevant; partner key rotation belongs to Control Plane.
strengths: Standards-based SCIM with Control Plane principals is better; never adopt a secret-in-path admin gate.
